Eh, this happens every few years. It's just not that common because a series of unlikely events has to happen: The game not only has to be mathematically impossible to effect the final playoff standings, so it realistically only has a short window at the end of the season where such conditions could exist. Even a team way ahead in the standings playing a losing ball club doesn't meet those mathematical requirements until near the end of the year. It also has to start but conditions for it to finish prove impossible - so a game where bad weather rains the game out doesn't count. The game must begin play and be suspended.

Really the rule is pretty simple, straightforward, and makes perfect sense. Enough innings had been played that a winner would have been declared had either team led, so even fans with tickets can't get too mad that they missed out on baseball. It's just a rare fluke thing.
